resolved_during_session.triage_note: Rewrite rules for mvs_battles_page / mvs_challenges_page / mvs_tournaments_page / mvs_compete_page persist in wp_options.rewrite_rules after Pro is deactivated (WP core does not auto-flush rewrites on plugin deactivation), but no query-var handler exists in Free to intercept them once Pro's classes are gone, so WP's main query falls through to the blog-home archive instead of issuing a 404. Confirmed this is specific to the reserved slugs, not a generic stale-cache artifact: a control URL /media/this-does-not-exist-xyz123/ correctly returns 404. Free's own mvs_media_slug rewrite regex explicitly excludes these words via negative lookahead `(?!battles|challenges|tournaments|leaderboard|edit-profile|page|compete/)`, i.e. Free already reserves them for Pro -- the gap is that nothing falls back to a 404/clean message when Pro isn't there to claim them. Not fatal, no dead/broken MVS UI rendered (satisfies the runbook's 'NOT fatal, NOT an empty broken shell' bar), but not a clean 404 either -- a customer who deactivates Pro and revisits a bookmarked /compete/ or /media/battles/ link silently gets unrelated site content at HTTP 200, which is confusing UX and a minor duplicate-content/SEO concern.
resolved_during_session.expected: /compete/, /media/battles/, /media/challenges/, /media/tournaments/ should either 404 or render a clean 'feature unavailable' fallback when Pro is inactive -- per runbook FREE-MODE FOCUS #3 ('should 404 or cleanly fall through, NOT fatal, NOT render an empty broken shell').
resolved_during_session.actual: All 4 URLs return HTTP 200 and silently render the site's default blog-home archive content (body class 'home blog...', the site's 'Hello world!' post, <title>buddynext</title>) instead of 404 or a plugin-owned fallback. No MVS markup, no fatal, no console error.
resolved_during_session.resolution: FIXED same session on the 2.3.2 branch: wpmediaverse-pro af7737c. Deactivation now deletes the rewrite_rules option (deferred rebuild on the next request, when Pro is gone) plus mvs_pro_rewrite_version (so reactivation re-flushes). Re-verified live by the calling session: pro off -> /media/battles|challenges|tournaments/ 404, /media/ unaffected; pro on -> all compete routes 200. The /compete/ PAGE persisting after deactivation is standard WP plugin-created-page behavior, not part of this defect.
